gen-nixie-one-gf-noto-sans-new-tai-lue: Noto Sans New Tai Lue has round, cupped letters that feel modern and unfussy. But Nixie One is the real oddity here, a display face whose line stays ruler-straight in weight while the body's shapes stay soft.
gen-nixie-one-gf-noto-sans-old-south-ara: Nixie One draws its heading in a hairline-steady stroke that leaves a soft, featureless hum across the line, while Noto Sans Old South Arabian lands friendly beneath it. Approachable, with curves that finish before turning inward.
gen-nixie-one-gf-noto-znamenny-musical-n: Noto Znamenny Musical Notation keeps its terminals stopping well away from the stem. Nixie One cuts its heading strokes like ribbon of constant width, so the two sit together as a thin, crisp top and a body that breathes beneath it.
gen-nixie-one-gf-palanquin: Contemporary in feel, Nixie One holds its thickness steady right around every curve of the heading. Palanquin follows underneath in sans-serif form, its wide, unclosed mouths giving the page an easy, professional footing.
gen-nixie-one-gf-rosario: Bent-wire lettering, thin and unvarying, is what Nixie One brings to the heading. But Rosario takes over below as a plain sans, its c-shaped ends never curling inward, so the page feels approachable and current.
gen-nixie-one-gf-sn-pro: Nixie One draws contrast-free strokes from stem to terminal, giving headings a wiry look. If it were made small, those hairline-feeling lines would fade, while SN Pro's open apertures hold up fine at body sizes.
gen-nixie-one-gf-teachers: Thin steel rod, bent into every letter: that is Nixie One, a display face of wiry, even lines. It does that look best, while Teachers is the one with ink strokes that taper out before touching.
gen-nixie-one-gf-telex: Nixie One gives the heading thin-looking letters with no thinner parts anywhere along them. Telex sits next to that in clean sans-serif form, its curvy letters feeling unclamped and a touch softer by comparison.
gen-nixie-one-gf-titillium-web: Approachable is the first thing Titillium Web says, its stroke ends set far apart. Nixie One, meanwhile, shows no brush-style swell anywhere in the heading, and over a long passage the body stays easy and open.
gen-nixie-one-gf-tomorrow: Clean lines come first from Nixie One, which does heading work best with its constant, pen-pressure look. And Tomorrow handles the text best, with bowls that open like a cupped palm of clay.
